govdocs-archive_org-nsia-OurDailyBread_O: This item — The Poultryman, January 7, 1966 — is a trade paper. The poultry trade had its own press. The issue is a curiosity. The file belongs to the business archive. The item is a fragment of publishing history.
the-history-of-a-mouthful-of-bread: French educator Jean Macé traces a mouthful of bread from the wheat field to the human body — a delicious lesson in science for young readers. His charming popular science made learning a genuine pleasure. A classic of nineteenth-century children's nonfiction.
five-little-peppers-abroad: Margaret Sidney takes the beloved Pepper family abroad in this cheerful series installment. Polly, Joel, Davie, Phronsie, and Ben discover Europe's wonders with their usual good spirits. Young readers loved traveling with the Peppers — wholesome family adventure at its best.
the-purple-land-being-the-narrative-of-o: W. H. Hudson's romantic novel follows Richard Lamb through the Banda Oriental — the wild Uruguay of the nineteenth century. Love, danger, and the purple-flowered land itself fill this sunlit adventure. Hudson's love for South America glows on every page.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-abraham-woodh: A 1913 Catholic Encyclopedia entry on Abraham Woodhead — the learned English controversialist of the penal times. His books defended the old faith with quiet power. Edwin Burton honors this scholar of the catacombs age. A recluse whose pen fought for Rome.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-allahabad: This 1913 reference piece on Allahabad — the Indian diocese at the holy rivers' meeting. Manoel D'sa gives its mission story. The Ganges and Jumna join below its walls. The Church grows in the ancient city. Faith at the sacred confluence. Its high court serves the province.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-arad: This 1913 reference article on Arad — a name in the eastern church story. The entry preserves its modest record. The old registers keep its name. The missions remember their stations. A station of the eastern missions. Its church serves the local faithful.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-bagdad: A 1913 entry on Bagdad — Baghdad, the Chaldean patriarch's see. Sophrone Pétridès tells its storied past. The caliphs' city kept the faith. The Tigris guards its ancient walls. The Rome of the Chaldean Church. Its patriarch rules the Chaldean flock.
